children: , Google's search, advertising, cloud and AI parent, challenged two European Union orders aimed at opening its services to rivals. Shares fell to $337.825 at 10.02 am ET time in Tuesday trading. The fight goes straight to Google's advantage: who gets access to Android's AI features and the search data that helps make its products better.

The European Commission's measures would give competing AI assistants access to Android features used by Gemini and let eligible search rivals obtain anonymized query, ranking, click and view data. Google says the requirements put privacy and security at risk. Regulators say the measures include safeguards.

For investors, the question is whether rivals can turn that access into products people actually use. Google's appeal keeps that question open while the legal fight plays out. At $337.825, the shares sit 33.79% above the chart's GF Value of $252.50, leaving less room for disappointment if Europe's rules weaken the ties between Android, Gemini and Search.

title: Alphabet Stock Slips as Google Appeals EU AI-Access Orders
